title: Optical-to-Thermal Pipeline for Multifunctional Plasmonic Metasurfaces: An AI-Agent Workflow from Multilayers to Three-Dimensional Nanoparticle Clusters
content: Plasmonic metasurfaces and photonic multilayers are increasingly designed to perform optical and thermal functions at once, but predicting the temperature of a real device requires bridging nanometric field hot spots and millimetric substrates, and full-wave models of this chain are slow to set up and can fail without any visible sign. Here, an optical-to-thermal pipeline driven by an AI agent is presented. From a plain-language description of the system, the agent writes the case files of three COMSOL Multiphysics templates (particles and clusters, multilayers, device transients), selects and cites the optical data, plans the mesh for the memory of the computer on which the simulations run, and accepts a result only when it meets a quantitative criterion against an independent reference (Mie theory, transfer matrix, coupled dipoles, analytic and finite-volume heat transfer) and passes convergence probes. On a 16 GB desktop computer, the full-wave cross sections and temperatures agree with the exact references within 0.35%, and on new requests the agent reached verified results at the first COMSOL run. The pipeline is applied to multilayer absorbers, nanosphere arrays, nanorods and three-dimensional nanoparticle clusters, showing that collective heating dominates whenever Baffou’s parameter is small and that single-time-constant models misestimate the photothermal kinetics.
